story.headline: No. 10 Wake Forest visits Georgia Tech, looking to take step toward ACC championsip game
paragraphs: Wake Forest can clinch its first trip to the Atlantic Coast Conference championship game since 2021 with a win at Georgia Tech and help elsewhere.

If the No. 10 Demon Deacons (9-1, 6-1 ACC, No. 11 CFP) win, they will secure their spot in Charlotte if either No. 6 Miami beats Virginia Tech or No. 21 Louisville loses to Pitt on Saturday night. If Wake Forest wins but does not get either result elsewhere, it could still wrap up the bid with a victory over Duke in its Nov. 28 regular-season finale.
Wake Forest's No. 11 spot in the College Football Playoff rankings means the Demon Deacons currently occupy the final projected at-large power conference bid in the 12-team field.

“That’s something that is out of our control,” linebacker Aiden Hall said after the Deacs beat SMU. “We just want to keep winning every week. We can’t control who recognizes us or who don’t, the only thing we can control is how bad we keep whuppin’ on teams.”

story.headline: No. 5 Miami to host Virginia Tech on Saturday, with ACC title game berth within reach
paragraphs: No. 5 Miami isn't deviating from its plan now.

It would take a collapse of epic proportions for the Hurricanes (9-1, 7-0 Atlantic Coast Conference, No. 7 CFP) to somehow miss out on a berth on the ACC title game. Miami can clinch its spot in that Dec. 5 game on Saturday with a win over Virginia Tech (6-4, 3-4).

And if it happens, don't expect some wild celebration. The Hurricanes have used the very simple approach of solely focusing on the current week all season long, with no indications that they will be changing course anytime soon.

“Just keeping our 1-0 mentality," Miami quarterback Darian Mensah said. "I feel like I talk about it all the time, but just focusing on what we’ve got this week, what we got (each day) at practice and trying to give our full energy and attention on right now and staying in the present.”

story.headline: No. 1 Georgia looks to take a step toward SEC history at No. 21 South Carolina
paragraphs: No. 1 Georgia looks to take another step toward a bit of Southeastern Conference history on Saturday night.

The Bulldogs (9-1, 7-1 SEC; No. 1 CFP) can clinch a spot in the final league championship game with a victory this weekend at No. 21 South Carolina (6-4, 4-4; No. 21 CFP). A win in Atlanta there in two weeks, and Georgia would be the last SEC championship game winner with the Power Four leagues giving up their postseason game for the expanded 24-team College Football Playoff.

Not that it will be easy. The Gamecocks and dynamic quarterback LaNorris Sellers enjoyed a magical month of Saturdays with four SEC victories including wins over ranked opponents in Florida and Tennessee before last week's dismal 34-6 washout to unranked Arkansas.
Sellers hurt his ankle in the win over Texas A&M and missed the loss at Arkansas. He's expected to be full go for the Bulldogs.

story.headline: No. 3 Notre Dame must battle emotions of Senior Night as well as SMU
paragraphs: Notre Dame will honor its seniors on Saturday when the No. 3 Fighting Irish take on unranked SMU, but the homefield farewell could extend beyond the seniors.

It could also be the final home appearance for a number of talented Fighting Irish juniors who may consider entering the NFL draft, including quarterback CJ Carr, cornerback Leonard Moore, linebacker Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa, safety Tae Johnson and defensive end Bryce Young. Offensive lineman Anthonie Knapp, linebacker Jaiden Ausberry and defensive lineman Francis Brewu have also appeared in the NFL draft projections.

Although CFP rankings, the emotions of a Notre Dame Stadium farewell and the prospect of NFL futures are swirling around the Fighting Irish, Notre Dame center Ashton Craig said the players can handle the emotions of the moment and still focus on the challenge of playing SMU (7-3, 5-3 Atlantic Coast Conference).

story.headline: No. 2 Utah visits TCU, close to Big 12 title game berth with Scalley part of all 10-0 starts
paragraphs: Morgan Scalley was a part of the previous two Utah teams that won their first 10 games, as a senior defensive back for the Utes in 2004 and then four years later in his first season as a full-time assistant coach.

Now in Scalley's first season as head coach at his alma mater, after never leaving through all those years, the No. 2 Utes (10-0, 7-0 Big 12, No. 2 CFP) can clinch a spot in the Big 12 Conference's final championship game with a win at TCU (5-5, 3-4) on Saturday night. The berth could be clinched if No. 12 BYU loses at Kansas earlier in the day.

“You care about the things that shape you, the things that have made you, things that have taught you so many valuable lessons here,” Scalley said about the long wait to be head coach and what it means in this moment. “A lot of memories of me growing up, going to games, obviously playing here, lessons learned from being here. Just want to be in a position to pass that on.”

The Utes, seeking their first College Football Playoff berth, have won their last 16 games, the longest active FBS streak. That includes the Las Vegas Bowl last New Year's Eve after the longtime defensive coordinator replaced departing coach Kyle Whittingham.
